prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every homeowner — the right one depends on your exact needs (roof size and type, budget, timing, insurance involvement, warranty expectations, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. Quick guidance and next steps:

How to find the best roofer in Dallas
- Get at least 3 written estimates from local, reputable contractors.
- Check online reputation: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, and BBB ratings. Read recent reviews about similar jobs (full replacements).
- Verify company basics: local physical address, active business registration, proof of general liability insurance and workers’ compensation (or signed indemnity if they don’t carry WC).
- Ask if they are certified installers for major shingle manufacturers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning). Manufacturer certification often improves warranty options.
- Confirm they will pull required city permits and perform code-compliant work.
- Ask for references from recent Dallas-area roof replacements and call them.
- Get detailed written estimate(s) with scope of work, materials, brand/model, tear-off vs. overlay, disposal, timeline, and payment schedule.
- Check warranties: material manufacturer warranty vs. workmanship/installation warranty from the contractor. Get warranties in writing.

Red flags to avoid
- Door-to-door storm chasers pressuring immediate signing.
- No written contract or vague scope of work.
- Large upfront cash-only payment (reasonable deposit 10–30% is common).
- Company won’t provide proof of insurance or references.

Typical price ranges (Dallas, ballpark)
- Asphalt shingle full replacement (average home): roughly $6,000–$15,000 depending on roof size, pitch, number of layers, and shingle quality.
- Upgraded shingles, metal, tile, or steep/complex roofs: $15,000–$40,000+.
(Exact price depends on your roof area, underlayment, flashing, decking condition, and labor.)

If you want a short list of well-reviewed Dallas roofers
Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you have a preferred material (asphalt shingle, metal, tile) and I’ll put together a short list of highly-rated local companies and questions to ask each.

If you’re dealing with insurance/ storm damage
- Document damage with photos, get a licensed contractor estimate, and coordinate with your insurance adjuster.
- Consider bringing the contractor to the insurance inspection to point out damage and necessary repairs.

Would you like me to: (A) recommend 3–5 specific Dallas companies (I’ll need your ZIP), (B) draft an email or checklist to send to contractors, or (C) help estimate cost from roof photos and dimensions?
